content.question_text: What is the primary purpose of packaging an application into a Java Archive (JAR) file?

core_requirements: To give users a single file instead of a directory structure filled with class files.
To compress the files using the ZIP compression format.
acceptable_variations: Single file distribution, uses ZIP compression.

content.question_text: What tool do you use to create JAR files, and what is the general format/syntax of the command?

core_requirements: `jar options file1 file2 ...` (or `jar cvf jarFileName file1 file2 ...`)
acceptable_variations: jar tool, jar cvf name files

content.question_text: In the `jar` command, what do the `c`, `v`, and `f` options do?

core_requirements: `c`: Creates a new or empty archive and adds files to it.
`f`: Specifies the JAR file name as the second command-line argument.
acceptable_variations: c = create, v = verbose, f = file name.

content.question_text: What is the specific name and directory location of the manifest file inside a JAR archive?
If you want to update the manifest of an existing JAR file with additions from a text file, which two `jar` command options must you use together?

core_requirements: `m` (Adds a manifest to the JAR file / modifies it)

content.question_text: What are the two ways to specify the main class (entry point) for an executable JAR file?

core_requirements: Use the `e` option in the jar command (e.g., `jar cvfe ...`).
Specify `Main-Class: com.mycompany.mypkg.MainAppClass` directly in the manifest file.
acceptable_variations: e option in command line, or Main-Class entry in manifest.

content.question_text: What crucial formatting caution must be followed when editing the last line in a manifest file manually?

core_requirements: The last line in the manifest must end with a newline character (line terminator).
Otherwise, the manifest will not be read correctly.
acceptable_variations: Must end with a newline/line break.

content.question_text: What command do users run to start a packaged program from the terminal?

acceptable_variations: java -jar followed by the file name

content.question_text: What is the sole purpose of multi-release JAR files?

core_requirements: To enable a particular version of your program or library to work with multiple JDK releases (backward compatibility).
acceptable_variations: To support different Java versions in the same JAR.

content.question_text: In a multi-release JAR file, where must the version-specific class files be placed?
According to JEP 293 (starting with Java 9), how should multiletter command-line options be formatted in Linux tools and modern Java tools?

core_requirements: Multiletter option names are preceded by double dashes (e.g., `--class-path`).
